introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (headed "One hour 30 minutes" on page 2): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (40 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (50 minutes): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 4 shows a simple circuit containing a device, D connected in series with a cell and a milliammeter.

![fig-1](gce-al-physics-2023-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_10_fig_1.png)

(i) What is the name of the device, D?

(ii) State and explain the steps that can be taken to cause the reading of the milliameter to rise.

(iii) What is avalanche breakdown? *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) D is a **photodiode** (a p-n junction diode in which light falling on the junction creates electron-hole pairs; the incident light is shown by the arrows).

(ii) Steps that make the milliammeter reading rise:

1. **Increase the intensity of the light** falling on D (or bring the source closer, or use a brighter lamp). More photons are absorbed in the depletion region, each photon of energy $hf$ larger than the band gap creates one electron-hole pair, so more charge carriers are available and the current in the circuit increases roughly in proportion to the light intensity. This works whether the photodiode is used with reverse bias (its usual mode, the current being then the photocurrent) or with forward bias.
2. **Increase the p.d. applied across the diode**, by adding a cell or using a battery of larger e.m.f. As drawn, the plates of the battery appear to put D in forward bias, so a larger p.d. gives a (rapidly) larger forward current once the threshold of about $0.6\ \mathrm{V}$ is exceeded. (With reverse bias, a larger p.d. changes the photocurrent very little, so the light intensity is then the effective control.)

(iii) **Avalanche breakdown** is the sudden large increase in the reverse current of a reverse-biased p-n junction when the reverse p.d. reaches the breakdown voltage. The strong electric field across the depletion layer accelerates the few minority carriers so much that they ionise atoms of the lattice by collision, releasing new electron-hole pairs; these are accelerated in turn and release more, so the number of carriers multiplies like an avalanche and the current rises sharply while the voltage across the diode stays almost constant.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 5 is a graph showing the transfer characteristic of a bipolar junction transistor connected in the common emitter mode.

![fig-2](gce-al-physics-2023-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_10_fig_2.png)

(i) Explain the origin of $I_0$ shown on the graph.

(ii) What is the significance of the slope of this graph?

(iii) Draw a diagram of a circuit in which this transistor is functioning as a light-operated switch. Such a switch turns lights on when the intensity of the light in the environment is low. Explain why this switch comes on when the light intensity is low. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) $I_0$ is the **collector current when the base current is zero**, $I_b = 0$: the **leakage current** $I_{CEO}$. The collector-base junction is reverse biased, and thermally generated minority carriers cross it, giving a small reverse (leakage) current $I_{CBO}$. With the base open, this current flows into the base region and is amplified by the transistor, so
$$I_0 = I_{CEO} = (\beta + 1)\,I_{CBO}.$$
It increases with temperature.

(ii) The slope $\dfrac{\Delta I_c}{\Delta I_b}$ is the **(small-signal) current gain $\beta$ of the transistor in the common emitter mode** ($h_{fe}$): the change of collector current produced by a given change of base current. Because $I_c$ is in $\mathrm{mA}$ and $I_b$ in $\mu\mathrm{A}$, the number read from the graph is $\beta/1000$ and must be multiplied by $1000$ to obtain $\beta$. A steeper line means a greater amplification.

(iii) **Circuit (to be drawn by the candidate).** Take an npn transistor with its emitter joined to the $0\ \mathrm{V}$ rail.

- A **potential divider** is connected between the $+V_s$ rail and $0\ \mathrm{V}$: a fixed resistor $R$ from $+V_s$ to the base, and a **light-dependent resistor (LDR)** from the base to $0\ \mathrm{V}$.
- The **lamp** (or a relay coil with a diode in parallel with it, the relay switching the lights) is connected between $+V_s$ and the collector.

**Explanation:** the resistance of the LDR is large in the dark (low light intensity) and small in bright light. In low light, the LDR takes most of the supply p.d., so the p.d. between base and emitter rises above about $0.6\ \mathrm{V}$. A base current flows, the transistor turns on (it saturates), a large collector current flows through the lamp and the lamp comes on. In bright light the resistance of the LDR is small, the base p.d. is below $0.6\ \mathrm{V}$, the base current is zero, the transistor is off and the lamp is off.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A two-door car has a safety light bulb that comes on when any of the doors is open.

(i) Complete the table below to show whether the bulb "lights" or "doesn't light"

| Door 1 | Door 2 | Bulb |
|---|---|---|
| Closed | Closed | |
| Open | Closed | |
| Closed | Open | |
| Open | Open | |

(ii) Taking closed door for low input and bulb lights for high output, draw a truth table for the system.

(iii) Give the name of the logic gate depicted by this system. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The bulb comes on when **any** door is open:

| Door 1 | Door 2 | Bulb |
|---|---|---|
| Closed | Closed | doesn't light |
| Open | Closed | lights |
| Closed | Open | lights |
| Open | Open | lights |

(ii) With closed = $0$ (low), open = $1$ (high), bulb lights = $1$, doesn't light = $0$:

| Door 1 (A) | Door 2 (B) | Bulb (Q) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 0 | 1 |
| 0 | 1 | 1 |
| 1 | 1 | 1 |

(iii) The output is high when A **or** B (or both) is high: the system is an **OR gate** ($Q = A + B$).
